To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the variance of each dimension of the embedding vector is a good regularization term for preventing a collapse in self-supervised methods; (2) the invariance of the covariance matrix is a good regularization for decorrelating the embedding variables; (3) our method, VICReg, achieves results on par or better than the state of the arts in self-supervised learning.

(1) the collapse problem in contrastive learning can be prevented with two regularizations, one on the variance and the other one on the covariance of the embedding vectors; (2) the variance regularization term is a simple, effective and generic technique to improve the training stability of other contrastive learning methods.

1) the collapse problem is caused by a loss of variance and a lack of covariance structure in the embeddings; 2) the collapse can be avoided by regularizing the variance and covariance of the embeddings; 3) the variance and covariance can be regularized by applying the regularization terms to the embeddings themselves, without the need for additional techniques such as weight sharing, feature normalization, memory banks, or stop gradients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How can we prevent a collapse in self-supervised methods?
the following questions: (1) Can a simple method that does not require any of the techniques mentioned above achieve results on par with state of the art methods?
the following questions: (1) Can we learn image representations that are invariant to transformations and covariate shifts, while preserving their variance?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VICReg can be used as a drop-in replacement for the loss function of other self-supervised methods, without the need for any of the above-mentioned techniques.
VICReg provides a simple and effective solution for the collapse problem in self-supervised learning.
VICReg is a simple and effective regularization technique that can be applied to any method to improve its performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a simple and effective regularization method that can be used as an alternative to the aforementioned techniques, and that can also be applied as a complementary technique to further improve the performance of other approaches.
VICReg can be applied on top of any other self-supervised learning framework to improve its performance.
VICReg is a simple, flexible and effective method for self-supervised learning that is easy to implement and can be combined with other methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple and effective regularization can be obtained from the properties of the embedding vectors themselves, rather than by introducing complex architectures and techniques that make the learning process more complicated.
a collapse in the embedding vectors is a problem that should be explicitly addressed by regularization.
the collapse problem in self-supervised learning can be solved by explicitly preventing the encoders from producing constant or non-invariant vectors.
